A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work. All 14 pages, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C, were inspected and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations on three tasks, cumulative-learning experiments and a Twenty Questions study with eight human participants.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and human-study results, revises the AIME outcomes and adds Claude results to Table 3.

M1.justification: The fixed-experience and cumulative-experience procedures, policy derivation, memory management and experience representations in Section 3.2 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AIME 2025, Twenty Questions with the same 157 candidate words, and Who is Undercover. The human population and game scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Claude to the thinking-model comparison previously containing only o1 and DeepSeek-R1. Claude already appeared elsewhere, but its participation in this comparison is new. The shortened heading R1 denotes the retained DeepSeek-R1 comparator.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain unchanged, including temperature 1, five prior interactions, 32 test cases and 50 cumulative rounds. No protocol revision is documented for the replaced AIME scores or added Claude column.

E4.justification: The full-history versus derived-policy pilot, cumulative-learning and human comparisons, Section 4.6 analyses, and Appendix C role-name case study are retained. The added comparator does not introduce a new ablation or diagnostic question.

E5.justification: Section 3.2.2 retains three repetitions per cumulative-evaluation setting, and the uncertainty displays in the figures are identical. No new seed information, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests accompany the revised tables.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially revises the AIME finding. Without/with experience-derived policy, GPT-4o changes from 0.0000/0.0667 to 0.0792/0.0542, Claude 3.5 Sonnet from 0.0333/0.0667 to 0.1417/0.1417, and DeepSeek-V3 from 0.4333/0.3333 to 0.2750/0.2458. Thus no evaluated model now improves on AIME. Table 3 adds Claude scores of 0.10, 0.10 and 0.20 for no policy, test-time policy and human policy. Existing o1 and R1 values are equivalent after rounding; game and human-study results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and cumulative-reward equations (1)–(2) are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, proofs or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion and numbered findings retain their claims about semantic-game evaluation, measurable but unstable LLM learning, and faster human learning. The AIME revisions do not lead to revised claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of policy quality, diminishing returns and model–human differences remain unchanged, as do the stated limitations concerning task breadth, human participation and parameter updates. No interpretation of the revised AIME results or added Claude column is supplied.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, output-format instructions, appendix game rules and policy examples, and code/data access information are unchanged. No additional configuration details are provided for the Claude column added to Table 3.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works and positioning against test-time training, in-context reinforcement learning and self-evolution are unchanged.

P1.justification: Textual edits are limited to the arXiv version/date stamp and shortening the Table 3 heading from DeepSeek-R1 to R1. The narrative prose, section order and appendix text are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains a Claude column, uses two decimal places instead of four, and has corresponding spacing and emphasis adjustments. The figures, other table structures and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added Claude comparison modestly broadens the evidence, but v2 introduces reporting inconsistencies. Its GPT-4o AIME change is listed as -30.57%, although the displayed scores imply approximately -31.57%, beyond a rounding discrepancy. Section 4.5 still describes only o1 and R1 despite the added Claude column, and the revised AIME finding receives no updated discussion. These are limited losses in reporting quality; the main framework, game evaluations and human study remain intact.
